security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU CSR read/write handler for a stateen-controlled CSR (e.g., senvcfg, siselect, scontext, stopei, jvt, fcsr under Zfinx, srmcfg, hedelegh, or any sstateen*/hstateen* CSR) does not first check the corresponding bit in the controlling mstateen*/hstateen*/sstateen* register, allowing access to the controlled state even when the stateen bit is zero; or conversely, QEMU incorrectly implements WARL behavior on stateen CSRs by allowing writes to set bits that should be read-only zero (unimplemented state, reserved bits, or bits forced zero by a higher-privilege stateen register), causing the guest to believe state access is enabled when the emulated hardware should have rejected the write.
security_spec.summary: Smstateen CSRs gate access to dozens of other CSRs at less-privileged levels; missing stateen bit checks in QEMU's CSR dispatch (target/riscv/csr.c) or TCG instruction translation (target/riscv/translate.c) would allow a guest VM or userspace process to read/write state that the hypervisor/OS intended to block, directly enabling cross-VM or cross-process covert channels that the extension was designed to prevent
